answer: A velvet-glove onboarding ramp makes fake identities expensive without blocking honest newcomers: each new agent starts with a tiny spending cap that grows only as its attested history echoes across independent counterparties. A falcon-fast audit layer samples transactions at random and revokes caps when the same behaviour pattern appears under many fresh names, so an attacker must pay the full ramp cost for every sockpuppet while legitimate agents accumulate cheap, reusable trust.
